title: Performance regression starting from 7.8.0 when too many search requests closes before getting result

labels.name: :Distributed/Task Management
labels.description: Issues for anything around the Tasks API - both persistent and node level.

body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`):
`7.10.2`

**Plugins installed**: []

**JVM version** (`java -version`):
```
openjdk 15.0.1 2020-10-20
OpenJDK Runtime Environment AdoptOpenJDK (build 15.0.1+9)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM AdoptOpenJDK (build 15.0.1+9, mixed mode, sharing)
```

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system):
`Linux HOSTNAME 3.10.0-1160.31.1.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Thu Jun 10 13:32:12 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:
After the upgrade of the ES from 7.6.2 to 7.10.2 one of our clusters become degraded a lot in terms of latency and throughput. After a big and long investigation, I [found the suspect](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/61e5350e770966172cd64430661eeb903bc94518). It looks like starting from 7.8.0, we have this performance regression, even in the latest 7.13.3.
Our cluster has a unique workload that is used mainly for testing purposes. We are evaluating ElasticSearch as a DB backed for our app, and to gather some performance metrics in the long run, we have a "shadow traffic," which has mirror requests from our production app to ES, but if the gateway can get a response faster from its main data source than from ES, it will close request, and Nginx shows that as 499 status code. As a side-effect, I can't use almost any /_cat API requests. This is the example:

```
$ > time curl -sS localhost:9200/_cat/tasks | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c
0.01user 0.15system 6:01.05elapsed 0%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 1232maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (0major+350minor)pagefaults 0swaps
 256591 cluster:admin/tasks/cancel
   2243 cluster:admin/tasks/cancel[n]
     23 cluster:monitor/nodes/info
     39 cluster:monitor/nodes/stats
      1 cluster:monitor/stats
     18 cluster:monitor/tasks/lists
     83 cluster:monitor/tasks/lists[n]
 121370 indices:data/read/msearch
 121370 indices:data/read/search
     10 indices:data/read/search[can_match]
      3 indices:data/read/search[phase/fetch/id]
    141 indices:data/read/search[phase/query]
   2243 internal:admin/tasks/ban
``` 

While cluster has a load of search requests - I can't get much from it. Latency skyrockets from 400ms(99 percentile) to 20seconds - 120seconds ( 99percentile ) 


**Steps to reproduce**:

I was able to write [simple script](https://gist.github.com/libbkmz/199891acb668f6fff6a677d47f29b85d) which can reproduce the issue, unfortunately, one active instance is not enough, and to simulate our real production shadow workload, I have had to run 5 instances to get stuck in [setBan method](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/v7.10.2/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/tasks/TaskManager.java#L354). Also, I'm attaching java flame graph captured by async-profiler for this particular problem. [es_setban_bug.flamegraph.html.gz](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/6812577/es_setban_bug.flamegraph.html.gz)

Moreover, I don't know how good our search query parameters, but this one is very intensive, and we have a lot of queries like this, and I'm able to reproduce the issue with such a simple script. 

Our cluster has 83 nodes in total, with 73 of data nodes, 3 master nodes, and 6 proxy nodes. However, we found some issues with our hardware, and we were using only 1 proxy node for more than 2 months. So, all the ES requests come to a single ES instance with flags `it` only on version 7.10.2. But using more than 1 proxy node doesn't help at all - the outcome is the same...
